predecessors.name: Republic of Venice
predecessors.text: the city of Ragusa and its district, under Venetian overlordship since the Fourth Crusade, until the Treaty of Zadar forced Venice 'to yield all claims to Dalmatia'

successors.name: First French Empire
successors.text: the whole republic, occupied by France from 27 May 1806 and abolished by Marshal Marmont's proclamation of 31 January 1808

ledger.x: 1358: the Treaty of Zadar forces Venice to give up Dalmatia and the Republic of Ragusa is established under Hungarian overlordship.
1403: war with Bosnia over the Primorje.
1404: the war ends with the Bosnian withdrawal; Ragusa keeps the Primorje.
1419: Ragusa buys eastern Konavle from Sandalj Hranic.
1426: Ragusa buys western Konavle, with Cavtat and Obod, from Radoslav Pavlovic.
1451: Herceg Stjepan attacks Ragusa for Konavle and besieges Dubrovnik.
1454: peace with the duke; Ragusa keeps Konavle.
1806: Russians and Montenegrins besiege French-held Ragusa.
1806: General Molitor appears in their rear and the Russian-Montenegrin forces abandon the siege; the siege period ends 1 October.
1808: Marshal Marmont abolishes the Republic of Ragusa.

wars.name: Ragusan-Bosnian war of 1403-1404
wars.outcome: 'ended with Bosnian withdrawal'; Ragusa kept the area between the city and Pelješac acquired in 1399.

wars.name: First Konavle War
wars.outcome: 'The First Konavle War lasted from 1430 to 1433'; the page does not say how it ended.

wars.name: War of Herceg Stjepan against Ragusa
wars.outcome: Stjepan Vukcic besieged Dubrovnik; the Ragusan government declared him a traitor; peace in 1454; Konavle stayed Ragusan.

wars.name: Siege of Ragusa (1806)
wars.outcome: 'French victory': the Russian-Montenegrin forces abandoned the siege after Molitor appeared in their rear; France abolished the republic in 1808.

certainty.note: The Primorje and Konavle frontiers with Bosnia are not fixed by a dated line until the purchases; Ston and Pelješac come from a 1325 sale and 1333 handover.
'Its final borders were formed by 1426'; the land frontier is fixed by purchase deeds and, from the 1699 Treaty of Karlowitz, by the two Ottoman buffer corridors at Neum and Sutorina.
